purpose: Evaluate whether general kick/snare rhythmic patterns learned from GMD can help bar-head selection on the three simpler 4/4 project songs, without changing kick/snare transcription events.

data.source: Google Magenta Groove MIDI Dataset raw MIDI, accessed through a public mirror preserving original MIDI files and info.csv split metadata.
data.warning: Earlier experiment using a third-party text conversion was discarded after an internal column-order inconsistency was found between midi_to_text.py/text_to_midi.py and raw MIDI examples.

hypotheses.name: fixed_backbeat_heuristic
hypotheses.description: Prefer typical kick beat 1/3 and snare beat 2/4 positions.

hypotheses.name: gmd_bar_weighted_global
hypotheses.description: Bernoulli likelihood from raw GMD 16th-grid kick/snare occupancy; bars weighted equally.

hypotheses.name: gmd_12_cluster
hypotheses.description: Nearest of 12 raw-GMD kick/snare groove templates.

hypotheses.name: gmd_discriminative_4bar
hypotheses.description: Structured linear 4-way rotation classifier trained on raw GMD 4-bar windows.

hypotheses.name: gmd_file_balanced_global
hypotheses.description: Global raw-GMD likelihood where each training performance contributes equal weight. Best auxiliary candidate.

conclusion.decision: Do not replace or override the current selector. Treat file-balanced GMD only as long-window auxiliary evidence after the existing snare-backbeat parity filter has reduced four candidates to the beat-1-vs-beat-3 pair.
conclusion.proposed_future_gate: Use >=16-bar evidence as a confidence/confirmation signal. If GMD disagrees with the acoustic selector, do not auto-override until failure cases demonstrate that such an override improves held-out project accuracy.
